markingScheme.criterion: Quotes the Balance number from BOTH the student's 'Only One Thing' day and their 'All Five' day (or otherwise clearly compares the two days using their own figures).
markingScheme.accept: Numbers copied from the student's own Investigation Record, with or without the % sign; two correctly quoted figures from the two named days. A clear own-data comparison such as 'my one-thing day was 31 and my all-five day was 88' earns this.
markingScheme.insufficient: Statements like 'one day was better' with no figures, or figures that do not appear in the student's own Record.

markingScheme.criterion: States which day was more balanced, consistent with their own figures (normally the All Five day).
markingScheme.accept: Any clear statement that the day looking after all five parts had the higher/better/more level balance, or that the one-part day was more wobbly or tilted.
markingScheme.insufficient: Naming a day that contradicts their own quoted numbers.

markingScheme.criterion: Gives a reason for the difference: parts that were left out got weaker or sank, and/or looking after one part also helped the parts linked to it.
markingScheme.accept: Any equivalent child-language reason, e.g. 'the other parts got low because Pip didn't look after them', 'they are connected so one helps the others', 'when you only did one thing the rest shrank'.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'Because it was better' or 'because I did more' with no mention of neglected or connected parts.

markingScheme.criterion: Identifies Sleep (going to bed very late, being tired) as the part Sam is leaving out.
markingScheme.accept: Sleep, rest, bedtime, being tired, not getting enough sleep.
markingScheme.insufficient: Naming Eating Well or Moving (Sam already does these), or no part named.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains a connection between being tired and feeling grumpy or arguing: tiredness makes it harder to stay calm or be kind to friends (the Calm Mind and/or Friends parts are affected).
markingScheme.accept: 'Being tired makes it hard to be calm', 'tired people get grumpy and argue', 'when you don't sleep you get upset with friends'. Naming Calm Mind or Friends as affected counts.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only that sleep is important, or only that Sam is grumpy, with no link between the two.

markingScheme.criterion: Suggests one sensible action Sam could take to help (e.g. an earlier bedtime or calming bedtime routine, screens off, breathing, asking an adult or friend for help).
markingScheme.accept: Any realistic, safe, helpful action connected to sleep, calming down or getting help. Hurtful actions earn no mark.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'Be nicer' or 'try harder' with no concrete action.
